t.1.193.2: Therefore I praise their virtues all the more, so that Vidura might not discern my intention from my gestures.
t.1.193.1: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: I too think of this exactly as you two do, but I do not wish to reveal my true feelings to Vidura.
t.1.193.3: And what you consider fitting, tell me that, Suyodhana; and you too, Rādheya, whatever you consider fitting, tell that to me.
t.1.193.5: Or else let King Drupada be tempted with great hoards of wealth, and his sons too, and all his ministers as well.
t.1.193.4: Today, through skilful brahmins who are well rewarded and trustworthy in their work, let us sow dissension between the sons of Kuntī and the two Pāṇḍavas born of Mādrī.
t.1.193.6: Abandon King Yudhiṣṭhira, the son of Kuntī, or else let them choose to make their dwelling right there.
t.1.193.7: Let them describe to each one separately their dwelling here as full of faults; thus divided, let the Pāṇḍavas set their minds on that very place.
t.1.193.8: Or else let some clever men, skilled in stratagems, divide the Pārthas from one another and turn them away from their mutual affection.
t.1.193.10: Or else, O king, let the death of Bhīmasena be arranged by concealed men skilled in stratagems, for he is the foremost of them in strength.
t.1.193.9: Or let them estrange Kṛṣṇā, for that is easily done since the husbands are many; or else let them set the Pāṇḍavas at odds with one another over her, and then turn her against them.
t.1.193.11: But once he is slain, O king, they will have lost their zeal and their vigor, and they will no longer strive for the kingdom, for he is their refuge.
t.1.193.12: For Arjuna is invincible in combat when Vṛkodara guards his back; without him, Phalguna in battle is not worth even a quarter of Rādheya.
t.1.193.14: Once the Pārthas have come here and are subject to our command, O king, we shall set about destroying them as we see fit.
t.1.193.13: Knowing their great weakness without Bhīmasena, and recognizing us as strong and themselves as the weaker, they will perish.
t.1.193.15: Or else let each son of Kuntī be enticed there by beautiful young women, and then let Kṛṣṇā become estranged from them.
t.1.193.17: Of these means, whichever one you consider to be free from fault, put that into practice before the time passes by.
t.1.193.16: Or else let Rādheya be sent to bring about their coming; then, after striking a pact with robbers, let them be slain by trusted agents.
t.1.193.18: As long as they have not yet placed their trust in Drupada, that bull among kings, just so long, even today, can they be overcome by you; but after that they cannot be overcome.
t.1.193.19: This, my dear friend, is my thought, and it inclines toward subduing them. Whether it is good or bad, what do you think, Rādheya?
